newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar plunges against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar plunges against dollar.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar plunged to a Friday closing of 482.00/483.00 per dollar as the Central Bank purposefully abstained from supplying the market with its usual steady flow of dollar sales, traders said.
The unit closed Thursday at 477.75/479.00 per dollar
"It looks, surprisingly, as though the Central Bank wants the bolivar to depreciate back to its central parity rate," said one trader.
Under a exchange bands system set up at the end of 1996, the Central Bank said it would depreciate a central parity rate for the bolivar at the rate of 1.32 percent per month.
The parity rate was set Dec. 30 at 472 bolivars, bringing bolivar parity for end-February to around 484 bolivars.
"Why didn't the bank intervene as it normally does?" said one broker. "It must have been because it didn't want to."
For most of the year a strengthening bolivar, bolstered by Central Bank intervention, has headed towards the system's lower band, set 7.5 percent below parity.
Traders said most of Friday's dollar demand stemmed from the interbank market, as banks covered short dollar positions.
